spec.description: The 10 m land cover of the whole planet, 2017 onwards (Impact Observatory, Microsoft and Esri, from Sentinel-2), drawn by the very ImageServer that measures the figures: two chosen years side by side on the map, the relative change by class, the composition year by year and what became what between the two years, for whatever the map shows or the area drawn on it.

options.content:
# Land use and land cover — Sentinel-2 10 m

The figures come from `computeHistograms`, which counts pixels per class over **the extent the map is showing**: pan or zoom, anywhere in the world, and everything below is recomputed in half a second.

**And the map now comes from that same service.** The background is the ImageServer drawing the land cover on demand, not a copy: map and numbers read one source, so they cannot drift apart.

**The two years of the comparison, on the map.** *Year A* and *Year B* choose which two years everything is measured between: the map carries one layer of each — A below, B on top — and the relative change down here is computed between exactly those two, not between the first and last of the series. Since B covers A, split the viewer with the first button in the map's control column to compare them: **Swipe** gives a vertical bar you drag from one year to the other. The composition by year, further down, still shows all nine.

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | [Sentinel-2 10m Land Use/Land Cover Time Series](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=cfcb7609de5f478eb7666240902d4d3d) · **Impact Observatory, Microsoft and Esri**. Licensed CC BY 4.0, anonymous access |
| Coverage | Worldwide, 10 m, nine classes, 2017-2025 |
| How it arrives | Figures: `computeHistograms` → Infinity. Background: `exportImage`, one request per tile, with the service's own palette |

**One service, not two hundred files.** An ImageServer is a *mosaic dataset*: the catalogue of its rasters, the rule for choosing between them, and a pyramid built over the whole set. That is why it answers for any extent at any zoom from a single endpoint — the entire planet in one layer, in little over a second per tile. The same collection split into COGs is some two hundred files per year, one per UTM zone.

**The years come from the source.** The selector carries no hand-written list: it asks the service's catalogue which years it publishes. They are the same nine the figures are measured over, with no drift.

**What you need to know so as not to misread the figures:**

- **Impact Observatory advises against pixel-by-pixel comparison between years.** Each year is classified separately and the model changes; part of the year-on-year difference is method, not territory. That is why this board leads with **relative change**, which holds up best.
- **The sampling runs on a Web Mercator grid, so area is biased by latitude.** Each sample covers `(scale·cos φ)²` of real ground: at 60° of latitude, a quarter of what it covers at the equator. The km² are **approximate**, and the more so — optimistically — for high-latitude classes the higher the view reaches. **Relative change does not carry that bias**, because all nine years are measured on the same grid.
- **The "Clouds" class is the year's quality thermometer.** When it rises, the rest of that year's classes are worth less. In testing it swings between 0.2 % and 1.8 % depending on the year and the region.

**Narrowing by drawing.** The map's draw tool (polygon or rectangle) replaces the view's extent with the shape: the figures come to describe only what the shape encloses, at the finest resolution the service allows. Delete the shape to go back to the view.

*The service cuts off at 4000 px a side and at ~13 M cells. Above 4000 it returns `{"histograms":[]}` **with no error**; above 13 M it returns an explicit 400. The hidden `scale` variable keeps the request at 3500 px a side, so neither ceiling should be reached.*


**A single class, with one click.** The **Land cover class** dropdown — or a click on the class in the relative-change gauge or in the detail table — leaves **both layers** showing that cover alone: the chosen class is common to both years, which is what lets you look at how it changed. The panel does not draw it: the service publishes a render function per class, and what arrives is the class in its colour with the rest of the raster **transparent**, so what shows underneath is the base map, not a hole. The figures do not move: they go on measuring **all** the classes, so that isolating is for looking and is not confused with filtering. Go back to *All* to recover the whole map.

**What became what.** The figures above count each year on its own, so they say how much each class grew or shrank, not what it turned into. *From Year A to Year B*, at the bottom, does: the server reads the raw class of the same ~65,000 cells of the view in both years (two requests to the same service, kept by the gateway) and counts the pairs, in km² of real ground, without the latitude bias. Rows are the class in A, columns the class in B; what stayed is left out. It is a sample of the view: a figure of a few cells is noise.

-- One service, not two hundred files.
--
-- The ImageServer is a mosaic dataset: the catalogue of its rasters, the rule for choosing
-- between them and a pyramid over the whole set. It answers for any extent at any zoom from
-- a single endpoint, so there is no block of UTM zones, no SAS signature and no tile server.
--
-- And it is the SAME service the figures below come from, so map and numbers cannot drift
-- apart: one source read twice. The mosaic rule picks the year.
SELECT
  'https://ic.imagery1.arcgis.com/arcgis/rest/services/Sentinel2_10m_LandCover/ImageServer' AS esri_url,
  '{"mosaicMethod":"esriMosaicAttribute","where":"Year=' || CAST($yearA AS VARCHAR) || '"}' AS mosaic_rule,

  -- Isolating a class: the service publishes one "Isolate ..." function per cover, which
  -- returns that class in its colour and EVERYTHING else transparent. Nothing is filtered
  -- or clipped here; the service is asked for another drawing. Empty means the cartographic
  -- renderer, the usual one.
  --
  -- `$cover` goes without quotes: this datasource quotes variables itself. It is matched
  -- loosely, so the selector's "Trees", a gauge's "Trees" and a table's "Trees km²" all work.
  CASE
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%tree%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Trees for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%rangeland%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Rangelands Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%crop%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Crops for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%built%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Built Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%bare%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Bare Ground Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%water%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Water Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%flooded%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Flooded Vegeation Areas for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%snow%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Snow or Ice for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%cloud%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Clouds for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    WHEN lower($cover) LIKE '%convert%'
      THEN '{"rasterFunction":"Isolate Converted Lands for Visualization and Analysis"}'
    ELSE ''
  END AS rendering_rule

spec.rawSql:
-- From year A (rows) to year B (columns), in km² of the current view or the drawn area.
-- computeHistograms counts each year on its own, so it cannot say what became what: this
-- reads the raw class of the same ~65,000 cells in A and in B (exportImage, format=bsq: one
-- byte a cell, then a mask) on a Web Mercator grid over the view, through the gateway's
-- cache, and counts the pairs. km² is each cell's real ground (a Mercator cell at 60° covers
-- a quarter of one at the equator), so these areas carry no latitude bias. A sample of the
-- view: a class covering a handful of cells is noise. The diagonal, what stayed, is left out.
SET VARIABLE lulc_mgrid = (
  WITH v AS (
    SELECT ST_GeomFromText(nullif(${area:sqlstring}, '')) AS g,
           try_cast(${mapWest:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE) AS w, try_cast(${mapEast:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE) AS e,
           try_cast(${mapSouth:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE) AS s, try_cast(${mapNorth:sqlstring} AS DOUBLE) AS n
  ), b AS (
    SELECT CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL THEN ST_XMin(g) WHEN coalesce(e, 180) <= coalesce(w, -180) THEN -180 ELSE coalesce(w, -180) END AS w,
           CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL THEN ST_XMax(g) WHEN coalesce(e, 180) <= coalesce(w, -180) THEN 180 ELSE coalesce(e, 180) END AS e,
           greatest(-80, CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL THEN ST_YMin(g) ELSE coalesce(s, -80) END) AS s,
           least(84, CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL THEN ST_YMax(g) ELSE coalesce(n, 84) END) AS n
    FROM v
  ), m AS (
    SELECT round(greatest(w, -180) * 20037508.342789244 / 180) AS x0, round(least(e, 180) * 20037508.342789244 / 180) AS x1,
           round(6378137 * ln(tan(radians(90 + s) / 2))) AS y0, round(6378137 * ln(tan(radians(90 + n) / 2))) AS y1
    FROM b WHERE e > w AND n > s
  ), g AS (
    SELECT *, greatest(1, least(4000, ceil((x1 - x0) / 10), round(sqrt(65536 * (x1 - x0) / (y1 - y0)))))::INTEGER AS nx
    FROM m WHERE x1 > x0 AND y1 > y0
  )
  SELECT {'x0': x0, 'x1': x1, 'y0': y0, 'y1': y1, 'nx': nx,
          'ny': greatest(1, least(4000, ceil((y1 - y0) / 10), round(65536 / nx)))::INTEGER}
  FROM g
);
SET VARIABLE lulc_murls = (
  SELECT list('http://feeds/lulc/exportImage?bbox='
      || g.x0::BIGINT || ',' || g.y0::BIGINT || ',' || g.x1::BIGINT || ',' || g.y1::BIGINT
      || '&bboxSR=3857&imageSR=3857&size=' || g.nx || ',' || g.ny
      || '&adjustAspectRatio=false&format=bsq&pixelType=U8&interpolation=RSP_NearestNeighbor'
      || '&renderingRule=%7B%22rasterFunction%22%3A%22None%22%7D'
      || '&mosaicRule=%7B%22mosaicMethod%22%3A%22esriMosaicAttribute%22%2C%22where%22%3A%22Year%3D' || y || '%22%7D'
      || '&f=image')::VARCHAR[]
  FROM (SELECT getvariable('lulc_mgrid') AS g),
       unnest([coalesce(try_cast(${yearA:sqlstring} AS INTEGER), 2017), coalesce(try_cast(${yearB:sqlstring} AS INTEGER), 2025)]) AS t(y)
  WHERE g IS NOT NULL
);
WITH classes(code, class, ord) AS (
  VALUES ('2', 'Trees', 1), ('B', 'Rangeland', 2), ('5', 'Crops', 3), ('7', 'Built area', 4), ('8', 'Bare ground', 5),
         ('1', 'Water', 6), ('4', 'Flooded vegetation', 7), ('9', 'Snow/Ice', 8), ('A', 'Clouds', 9)
), b AS (
  -- A list of hex digits: indexing it is constant time, a substring of a long string is not.
  SELECT regexp_extract(filename, 'Year%3D([0-9]{4})', 1)::INTEGER AS year, str_split(hex(content), '') AS h
  FROM read_blob(coalesce(getvariable('lulc_murls'), []::VARCHAR[]))
), g AS (
  SELECT unnest(getvariable('lulc_mgrid'))
), ab AS (
  SELECT (SELECT h FROM b WHERE year = coalesce(try_cast(${yearA:sqlstring} AS INTEGER), 2017)) AS ha,
         (SELECT h FROM b WHERE year = coalesce(try_cast(${yearB:sqlstring} AS INTEGER), 2025)) AS hb
), cells AS (
  SELECT ab.ha[2 * c.cell + 2] AS a, ab.hb[2 * c.cell + 2] AS b,
         6371.0072 ^ 2 * ((g.x1 - g.x0) / g.nx / 6378137)
           * (sin(2 * atan(exp((g.y1 - (c.cell // g.nx) * (g.y1 - g.y0) / g.ny) / 6378137)) - pi() / 2)
            - sin(2 * atan(exp((g.y1 - (c.cell // g.nx + 1) * (g.y1 - g.y0) / g.ny) / 6378137)) - pi() / 2)) AS km2
  FROM (SELECT unnest(range((SELECT nx * ny FROM g))) AS cell) AS c, g, ab
  WHERE ab.ha IS NOT NULL AND ab.hb IS NOT NULL
    AND (nullif(${area:sqlstring}, '') IS NULL
         OR ST_Contains(ST_GeomFromText(${area:sqlstring}),
                        ST_Point(degrees((g.x0 + (c.cell % g.nx + 0.5) * (g.x1 - g.x0) / g.nx) / 6378137),
                                 degrees(2 * atan(exp((g.y1 - (c.cell // g.nx + 0.5) * (g.y1 - g.y0) / g.ny) / 6378137)) - pi() / 2))))
), pairs AS (
  SELECT ka.class AS a, ka.ord AS a_ord, kb.class AS b, sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE cells.a <> cells.b) AS km2
  FROM cells JOIN classes ka ON ka.code = cells.a JOIN classes kb ON kb.code = cells.b
  GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT a AS "From ↓ · to →",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Trees') AS "Trees",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Rangeland') AS "Rangeland",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Crops') AS "Crops",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Built area') AS "Built area",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Bare ground') AS "Bare ground",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Water') AS "Water",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Flooded vegetation') AS "Flooded veg.",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Snow/Ice') AS "Snow/Ice",
       sum(km2) FILTER (WHERE b = 'Clouds') AS "Clouds",
       sum(km2) AS "Lost (all)"
FROM pairs
GROUP BY a, a_ord
ORDER BY a_ord

-- The years come from the service itself: its catalogue is a table with a Year field
-- (nine today, the same years the figures are measured over). Through the gateway, which
-- keeps the answer a day.
WITH resp AS (
  SELECT http_get(
    'http://feeds/lulc/query'
    || '?where=1%3D1&outFields=Year&returnDistinctValues=true'
    || '&returnGeometry=false&orderByFields=Year&f=json'
  ) AS r
),
rows AS (SELECT unnest(json_extract(r->>'body', '$.features[*]')) AS f FROM resp)
SELECT DISTINCT CAST(f->'attributes'->>'Year' AS VARCHAR) AS year
FROM rows
WHERE f->'attributes'->>'Year' IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY year DESC

WITH v AS (
  SELECT length('$area') > 8 AS drawn,
         try_cast('$mapWest' AS DOUBLE) AS w, try_cast('$mapEast' AS DOUBLE) AS e,
         try_cast('$mapSouth' AS DOUBLE) AS s, try_cast('$mapNorth' AS DOUBLE) AS n
), c AS (
  SELECT drawn,
         CASE WHEN drawn THEN ST_XMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN -180.0 ELSE coalesce(w,-180.0) END AS w0,
         CASE WHEN drawn THEN ST_XMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area'))
              WHEN coalesce(e,180.0) <= coalesce(w,-180.0) THEN  180.0 ELSE coalesce(e, 180.0) END AS e0,
         CASE WHEN drawn THEN greatest(-80.0134, ST_YMin(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(s,-80.0134))) END AS s0,
         CASE WHEN drawn THEN least(84.0326, ST_YMax(ST_GeomFromText('$area')))
              ELSE greatest(-80.0134, least(84.0326, coalesce(n, 84.0326))) END AS n0
  FROM v
), d AS (
  SELECT drawn, w0, e0, s0, n0,
         CASE WHEN e0 <= w0 THEN 360.0 ELSE least(360.0, e0 - w0) END AS dlon,
         (ln(tan((90 + greatest(n0, s0 + 0.0005)) * pi()/360))
          - ln(tan((90 + s0) * pi()/360))) / (pi()/180) AS dmerc
  FROM c
), e AS (
  SELECT *, greatest(dlon * 111319.490793 / 3500, dmerc * 111319.490793 / 3500, 10.0) AS scale FROM d
)
SELECT printf('%.4f', scale) AS scale FROM e
